stem:
Rohan pushes his steel tiffin box across two different table surfaces at home.
On the smooth glass dining table the box slides a long way before stopping. On the rough wooden study table it stops much sooner.
Which statement correctly explains why the box stops sooner on the wooden table?

options.text: Friction acts only after the box has stopped, so it pulls the box backwards on the wooden table.
The rough wooden surface has more irregularities, so it produces greater friction that opposes the motion and slows the box faster.
Friction is the same on both surfaces, but the box is heavier on the wooden table so it stops sooner.
The smooth glass surface produces more friction because the box moves faster on it.

teacher.key_rationale: Friction arises from surface irregularities and opposes motion; a rougher surface gives greater friction, so the moving box slows and stops more quickly. Only B states this correctly. A wrongly claims friction acts only after stopping, C wrongly treats friction as surface-independent, and D reverses the roughness–friction relationship.
